outcome: Prevalence of heart failure during pregnancy
cohort: 488 pregnant women with heart failure (identified from a cohort of 385,935 pregnancies) compared to those without heart failure
finding: Heart failure during pregnancy was associated with adverse fetal outcomes, including preterm birth and low birth weight, and a 7.7-fold increased risk of maternal death during a median follow-up of 6.2 years.
mod_finding: This study found that preterm birth and cesarean delivery were more common in pregnant patients with heart failure.
birth_weight: Lower in infants of mothers with heart failure (3112.0±774.0 g vs 3331.9±575.5 g, p<0.001)
